hook: Two boaters on a sailboat with no sail, in a tropical storm.
narration: Up to twenty foot seas, fifty knot winds, and two boaters on a sailboat that had lost its sail.
This was Tropical Storm Debby, seventy-three miles off Boca Grande, Florida.
They were sailing from Key West to Tarpon Springs, and they missed their check-in.
A search plane found the boat in the storm and guided in a Coast Guard Jayhawk helicopter.
A sailboat's mast can swing into a hoist cable, so crews often lift survivors from the water, clear of the boat.
One at a time, the hoist pulled them up out of the storm.
outcome: Both boaters reached Air Station Clearwater with no reported injuries.
title: Sailboat adrift in Tropical Storm Debby
question_comment: Would you sail between Key West and Tarpon Springs with a storm coming?

description:
Two boaters whose 34-foot sailboat lost its sail about 73 miles off Boca Grande, Florida, during Tropical Storm Debby on Aug. 4, 2024, were hoisted by an Air Station Clearwater MH-60 Jayhawk crew.
